blocks.content: Volcanic eruptions, while inherently destructive, act as crucial geological drivers that replenish soil nutrients, concentrate precious minerals, and generate massive geothermal heat.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Volcanic ash and weathered basaltic lava create highly fertile soils rich in iron, magnesium, and potash, such as the Black Cotton Soil (Regur) of the Deccan Plateau.
Subterranean heat from volcanic sources drives geothermal energy production, seen in Indian geothermal zones like Puga Valley in Ladakh and Manikaran in Himachal Pradesh.
Volcanic processes concentrate valuable deep-mantle minerals, including diamonds in kimberlite pipes, gold, copper, nickel, and elemental sulfur.
Geysers and thermal springs formed near volcanic regions create eco-tourism hubs and mineral baths prized for therapeutic qualities.
Extrusive igneous rocks such as basalt and pumice serve as major raw materials for road construction, concrete manufacturing, and industrial abrasives.

items: UPSC Prelims often test the origin of Black Soils (Regur Soil)—remember that they were formed by the weathering of basaltic lava from Cretaceous Deccan volcanic activity.
Match the Geothermal Fields: Puga Valley (Ladakh), Manikaran (Himachal Pradesh), and Tapovan (Uttarakhand) are frequently asked in competitive exams.
Kimberlite pipes, which are ultrabasic volcanic pipes, are the primary geological source of natural diamonds (e.g., Panna in Madhya Pradesh).
